records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:74 — [P2 confidence=100] A grant extension following OAuth2GrantTypeFactory's documented three-letter shortcut produces token IDs that this same provider rejects because `if (encodedContext.length() != 6)` requires exactly two grant characters while `grantShort +` in encodeTokenId writes the registered shortcut without length validation.
records.rationale: The finding claims that a custom grant using a three-character shortcut would be rejected by the decoder. Looking at the code in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java lines 68-85, the getTokenContextFromTokenId method checks `if (encodedContext.length() != 6)` and throws an exception. The encoded context is composed of sessionType shortcut (2 chars) + tokenType shortcut (2 chars) + grantType shortcut. The OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.getShortcut() javadoc says 'usually like 3-letters shortcut' but the decoder expects exactly 6 characters total, meaning grant shortcuts must be exactly 2 characters.

records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/protocol/oidc/encode/DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.java:113 — [advisory P2 confidence=100] Deploying a new grant with an existing shortcut executes `grantsByShortcuts.put(shortcut, grantType);` and silently reclassifies already-issued tokens as the new grant while retaining both forward mappings; the strongest rebuttal is the duplicate check in postInit, but this explicitly supported late-deployment path bypasses that check, so token-context consumers receive the wrong grant identity.
records.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a potential issue in the lazy registration paths at lines 113-117 (getShortcutByGrantType) and 125-133 (getGrantTypeByShortcut). When a new grant type is dynamically discovered, the code adds entries to both grantsByShortcuts and grantsToShortcuts maps without checking for duplicate shortcuts. The postInit method (lines 68-79) does validate that map sizes match to detect duplicates, but the lazy registration paths bypass this validation.
